children: Our Political Bureau Kolkata: The Adani Group is committed to invest over 1 lakh crore in West Bengal by 2035 with a focus on developing ports, logistics, power generation and distribution, highways, roads, bridges and data centres among others, Adani Group chairman Gautam Adani said in Kolkata on Thursday, while addressing a function on the occasion of laying the foundation stone for the Adani Arogya Mandir. "Bengal is the natural maritime and logistics bridge, connecting India's vast industrial heartland and the Northeast with the Bay of Bengal," Adani said. "Bengal is also best positioned to connect with the maritime trade routes deep into Southeast Asia and beyond which gives the state a structural advantage few regions can match and the potential to become not just a gateway but also one of Asia's greatest integrated industrial and economic platforms." The Arogya Mandir is a 2,000-bed hospital in New Town in Kolkata, for which a 'bhumi pujan' was conducted by Gautam Adani, his family members and chief minister Suvendu Adhikari.

He said the Arogya Mandir will be run on a non-profit basis, where 50% of the facilities would be for the economically weaker sections of people, who are eligible under state and central health insurance schemes. This facility, with 4,000-crore investments, will be developed into a medical hub with a medical college and a research centre.

Adani said West Bengal would become the Adani Group's 'Karambhumi' in eastern India, which he referred to as "the land of Vivekananda and Vande Mataram", and not just an investment destination. Adhikari urged Gautam Adani to extend his support to rebuild Bengal.

Adani described Mundra Port in Gujarat as the group's first 'Karambhumi'. "This great land will rise, will move forward and will be the steering force for the progress of the entire country," Adani said. "India is looking east once again with the hope that Bengal will write its next great chapter.

Adani wants to help build that chapter alongside the people of Bengal," he said. "This is the land of Rabindranath Tagore, Swami Vivekananda, Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose-a land whose ideas, courage, science, and culture have helped shape the destiny of our nation," Adani said. "The chief minister, yours is the story of a real Bhumiputra, a son of the soil, of whom the people of this state have a great expectation for jobs, for infrastructure, education, healthcare and opportunity, Adani said. "Under your leadership, I have every reason to believe Bengal will redefine the possibilities ahead." Adhikari said West Bengal had suffered first during the 34-year Communist rule, and then for 15 years under the Trinamool Congress. "The previous state government only believed in dole politics and appeasement politics. Now, since we have received a huge mandate, we request the Adani Group to support us in economically and industrially developing West Bengal," he said.

title: Adani Group may Invest 1 L cr in Bengal by 2035
